headline: Volume-led revenue growth, but rising costs cap earnings
summary_short: Revenue rose 19.0% y/y to $1,190M on higher trading volumes and institutional commissions, but diluted EPS slipped 1.2% to $1.63 as compensation and interest expense grew faster than revenue.
summary_long: Total revenue grew 19.0% y/y to $1,190M, led by a 31.2% rise in Trading income, net ($856.7M) on higher trading volumes, and a 16.6% rise in Commissions, net and technology services ($179.5M) on stronger institutional engagement, partly offset by the absence of last year's RFQ-hub sale gain. Operating expenses rose faster, up 29.8% to $847.4M, on higher employee compensation (+59.1%, discretionary incentive accruals), interest/dividends expense (+24.3%) and brokerage/clearance fees (+28.2%). Pretax income was roughly flat at $342.6M (-1.3% y/y); GAAP net income fell 2.7% to $284.9M as the tax rate rose to 16.8% from 15.6%. Diluted EPS fell 1.2% to $1.63 on a 2.4% rise in weighted diluted shares. The board declared a $0.24/share dividend; no forward guidance was issued.

'Net income (available to common)' is the resolver's net_income_usd_m ($150.9M), which is consolidated GAAP net income ($284.9M) net of noncontrolling interest allocation — both figures appear in summary_long for clarity; the two move differently y/y because the noncontrolling-interest allocation shrank y/y. Revenue, pretax income, EPS, cash, debt and equity are SEC-XBRL verbatim from the 10-Q; q/q/y/y priors for revenue and net-income-available carry Yahoo fundamentals-timeseries provenance per the resolver output. No forward revenue/EPS guidance was disclosed — Virtu, as a market maker, does not issue quarterly guidance ranges. Q2 share repurchases (31,840 shares, ~$1.6M) were entirely for employee tax-withholding on vested equity awards, not open-market purchases under the $1.72B buyback program (unused authorization unchanged at $302.8M through the quarter).

drivers.explanation: Higher trading volumes and institutional engagement drove revenue up, but incentive compensation, interest expense and a higher tax rate grew faster, leaving net income and EPS roughly flat to slightly lower.
Trading income, net rose $203.9M on higher trading volumes and opportunities across global markets; Commissions, net and technology services rose $25.6M on strengthened institutional engagement.
Operating expenses grew 29.8%, outpacing 19.0% revenue growth, on higher employee compensation (discretionary incentive accruals), interest/dividends expense and brokerage/clearance fees.
Consolidated net income fell 2.7% as the effective tax rate rose to 16.8% from 15.6%, but the noncontrolling-interest allocation also shrank, leaving the common-stockholder share roughly unchanged.
EPS fell slightly more than net income available to common because weighted diluted shares rose 2.4% y/y (85.5M to 87.6M).
Long-term debt rose y/y mainly from the September 2025 incremental $300.0 million Term B-2 Loan issuance used for general corporate purposes.
